hardware: Shared AMD EPYC 9V74 VM, 4-CPU quota; llvmpipe LLVM19 software Vulkan; no physical GPU
scope: Native general-3D scene, animation, rendering and present loop. No gameplay scripts, physics, audio, production assets or streaming.
method: Seven cases, two unprofiled runs each; five separate profiler-enabled runs. 60 warmup +90 measured frames, VSync off, hidden Xvfb Vulkan surface. Diagnostic timings are not pooled with unprofiled runs.

findings.evidence: Frame.SubmitPresent is 89-95% of profiled frame wall time. Lightweight CPU sampling assigns 91.26% of sampled CPU time to a software Vulkan worker subtree.
findings.action: On physical GPU, split pass timings and capture draw/triangle/skinning counts. Compare actor count, shadow cascades and instancing/batching before selecting an engine optimization.
findings.gain_bound: Not established: this environment is dominated by software rendering; do not treat wait duration as removable overhead.

findings.evidence: Mixed1000 profiled frame 102.414 ms: Render3D self wall 2.35809 ms, record/join self wall 1.63666 ms, graph compile 0.356438 ms, acquire 0.887494 ms. Workers can overlap these scopes.
findings.action: Separate record CPU work from scheduler/worker waiting; count draws/state changes and allocations in a steady-state window.
findings.gain_bound: Entire Render3D inclusive scope is about 5.34 ms in this case, roughly 5.2% of observed frame wall time; this is a budget, not promised recoverable time.

findings.evidence: Scene plus animation average wall time is below 0.7% of unprofiled frames in this matrix.
findings.action: Defer further small-function optimization in these paths until a representative CPU-bound workload or physical-GPU profile changes the ranking.
findings.gain_bound: Even eliminating the measured scene and animation stages would remove less than 1% of frame wall time here.

metadata.window_method: Middle 40% of measured-frame duration, counted backward from process exit; excludes setup/warmup and avoids final 30%. Teardown/collector exit offset is not separately measured.

sampling.main_thread_caveat: Only four 10ms CPU samples in the selected main-thread window; no fine-grained main-function ranking is justified. Profiler zone self time is wall time, not exclusive CPU consumption.

limitations: Software Vulkan shares CPU quota with the engine; results do not predict physical-GPU FPS or shader costs.
Two timing repetitions are exploratory, not statistical significance evidence. p95 values are per-run, not pooled-frame quantiles.
Sampling window is estimated from elapsed duration and measured-frame duration, not explicit in-engine markers. The selected call tree is runtime software-driver work.

Heavy heap/synchronization tracing timed out after 300 seconds. Its 120-180 second window still included SceneFixture construction and LLVM/driver setup; excluded from steady-state allocation, waiting and leak conclusions.
No steady-state allocation counts or upload-byte totals were established. Resolution/actor/shadow variations identify candidate workloads, not proof of specific GPU shader bottlenecks.
No hardware-GPU pass timestamps, triangle/draw counters or GPU occupancy data were available.
